basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 28.' and it opens '(Cap. XI.—Vers. 28.) Et mortuus est Aran ante patrem suum in terra, qua natus est in'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Cap. XI.—Vers. 28.) Et mortuus est Aran ante patrem suum in terra, qua natus est in regione Chaldaeorum. Pro eo, quod legimus, in regione Chaldaeorum, in Hebraeo habetur, in UR CHESDIM (כשדים באור), id est in igne Chaldaeorum. Tradunt autem Hebraei ex hac occasione, istiusmodi fabulam: Quod Abraham in ignem missus sit, quia ignem adorare noluerit, quem Chaldaei colunt, et Dei auxilio liberatus, de idololatriae igne profugerit: quod in sequentibus scribitur, egressum esse Tharam cum sobole sua de regione Chaldaeorum: pro quo in Hebraeo habetur, de incendio Chaldaeorum. Et hoc esse quod nunc dicitur: Mortuus est Aran ante conspectum Thare patris sui in terra nativitatis suae, in igne Chaldaeorum: quod videlicet ignem nolens adorare, igne consumptus sit. Loquitur autem postea Dominus ad Abraham: Ego sum qui eduxi te de igne Chaldaeorum.
